text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and tool outputs, the wording is mostly cautious, and the audit-trail findings are grounded. The summary falls short in four ways. The headline contradicts itself, saying charts support the billed levels but the notes look inflated. The rationale repeats itself. The cited claims are a weak sample, and the next steps are generic.","problems":["Headline is internally contradictory (\"Charts support billed levels\" vs \"notes look inflated\") and states inflation more strongly than the evidence supports; the body says \"suggests documentation written to match the bill\".","Rationale repeats the 24.2% vs 2.6% figures and the no-chart-below-billed point twice, so it is padded.","Only two cited examples (C0082819, C0082837), both low-complexity 99215s with no chart evidence. Those examples do not illustrate the note-quality findings, and flagged claims such as C0082883, C0082986 and C0082841 (bulk-created, paste-heavy, late) are not cited.","Next steps are generic: request a targeted sample of 99215 charts, starting with the two cited claims. They do not target the audit-trail-flagged notes or the 9 data-review claims with no lab on the claim, and the audit trail has already been received.","Recommends \"audit-trail review before any leaning\" although the audit trail was already received and summarized, which is inconsistent.","Does not mention that the 4 documented 99215 claims shown as supported include C0082872 with no recorded minutes, nor that documented 99215 supports billing in all 11 cases, which weakens the inflation framing.","\"17% are duplicates\" is mentioned without explanation or example claims."]}
